categories.main_business_segments: Concraft Holding Co., Ltd. primarily operates in the automotive parts and electronic connectors sectors. Its business includes the design, manufacturing, and sales of automotive components such as sensors, electric drive system modules, brake and air suspension parts, and transmission components. Additionally, the company produces electronic connectors used in notebooks, set-top boxes, LCD TVs, and servers, as well as molds and precision machining services. The company also has a semiconductor heat sink business segment.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technology centers on insert molding (embedding non-metal materials into plastic molds) and advanced mold design and manufacturing. It emphasizes automation in production, with 80-90% of assembly automation equipment self-developed. The firm continuously improves its insert molding process and integrates silicone injection molding for applications in acoustic, optical, and automotive components. Vertical integration includes mold development, plastic injection, stamping, electroplating (outsourced), and assembly.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Concraft serves Tier 1 automotive parts suppliers and electric vehicle brands, including global names like Bosch, UAES, Webasto, Brose, and Brose. Its automotive parts are used in electric vehicles, hybrid vehicles, and traditional vehicles, targeting markets in China, Europe, and the Americas. The electronic connectors serve industries such as telecommunications, consumer electronics, industrial production, military/aerospace, and automotive. The company has recently expanded into Chinese domestic new energy vehicle suppliers and well-known Chinese automotive brands.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in Greater China, with manufacturing facilities in Kunshan and Baoying, China, and sales and R&D offices in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Mauritius. Its main sales market is China, accounting for over 85% of revenue, with additional sales in Taiwan, the United States, and other regions. The company also targets global automotive markets including Europe, North America, and Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: Concraft operates mainly in the midstream segment of the automotive and electronics supply chain, manufacturing key components and modules for Tier 1 suppliers and OEMs. It is positioned as a component supplier providing precision parts and connectors, with capabilities in mold making and assembly automation, supporting upstream raw material processing and downstream vehicle assembly.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company focuses on developing differentiated, high-value automotive components, especially for new energy vehicles (electric, hybrid, fuel cell). R&D priorities include electric drive system components, silicone material applications, and semiconductor packaging materials. It invests in automation equipment design to reduce costs and improve production efficiency. The company plans to implement MES (Manufacturing Execution System) for enhanced production management and quality control.
categories.revenue_model: Concraft generates revenue primarily through product sales of automotive parts, electronic connectors, and precision molds. It also benefits from strategic investments and partnerships, such as in its semiconductor heat sink business. Revenue is derived from long product life cycles (5-10 years) and ongoing supply contracts with Tier 1 automotive suppliers and OEMs.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes with global Tier 1 automotive parts suppliers and connector manufacturers, including Bosch, Continental AG, and Denso. While it may not match the R&D scale of large international firms, Concraft differentiates itself through flexible, small-batch automated manufacturing and strong customer relationships. It holds strategic supplier status with major automotive brands and is expanding its footprint in the Chinese new energy vehicle market.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Concraft reported consolidated revenue of approximately NT$1.516 billion, a 9.98% decline from 2023, with a net loss of NT$149 million, improving from a larger loss in the prior year. The company’s revenue is primarily from automotive parts (over 95%). It has strengthened its capital base through private placements totaling NT$95.77 million in 2024. The company expects revenue growth in 2025 driven by new energy vehicle component sales and semiconductor heat sink products.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Concraft emphasizes product differentiation through advanced insert molding technology, automation, and flexible small-batch production to meet diverse customer needs efficiently. Its long product life cycles enable stable production planning and cost control. The company’s ability to integrate mold design, material innovation (e.g., silicone applications), and automated assembly provides competitive advantages in quality and cost. Strategic partnerships with Tier 1 suppliers and direct OEM supply qualifications enhance its market position.
